assessment: Final decision: retain both legacy and newer xTB engines to preserve existing scientific behavior. Passing feature tests does not establish numerical parity; gradient differences and Fe100 aligned RMSD of approximately 1.03 A rule out consolidation as a behavior-preserving size reduction. Audit complete; no further audit tests required.

packaging_recommendation.reason: Meaningful Cartesian gradient differences and a different Fe100 optimized conformation (aligned RMSD 1.0349 A) outweigh the proposed binary size savings when preserving scientific behavior is required.
packaging_recommendation.layout: Retain xtb_runtime/xtb.exe, libiomp5md.dll, legacy share/ parameters and notices, together with xtb_runtime/gfnff/xtb.exe, its required DLLs, licenses and runtime provenance.
packaging_recommendation.runner: Preserve original routing: legacy root executable for ordinary GFN1/GFN2; newer gfnff executable for GFN-FF and GFN1/GFN2 with exact Cartesian fixing. Consolidation fallback and associated tests were reverted by main.
packaging_recommendation.parameters: For newer executable set XTBPATH to its own gfnff directory, never legacy share/. Its built-in GFN-FF parameters expect 103 elements, legacy external file has 86.
packaging_recommendation.unchanged_limitations: GFN-FF solvation and spinpol/tblite are not exposed by the current application.
packaging_recommendation.distribution_slimming: Omit source archives from the distribution only; retain required binaries, parameter files and license notices. Keep source archives available in the source/build workflow.
packaging_recommendation.release_zip: Not inspected. No assumption that latest published ZIP contains gfnff.
packaging_recommendation.validation_status: Audit complete; no further audit tests requested. Main is rebuilding the original runner/tests. Recorded candidate suites remain experimental evidence, not approval to consolidate.
